name: Sunscorched Shell
summary: Beneath Highperch, wyvern eggs leave shells hardened by Thousand Needles' desert heat. Armorer Mathiel in Darnassus uses them to make lacquer for mail links.

sections.title: Desert Clutches
sections.body: Highperch wyverns lay eggs on the mesa needles of southern Kalimdor. Beneath their roosts, discarded shell fragments bake in the desert sun and searing winds. Their brittle remains hold a natural resilience that draws the attention of skilled artisans.

sections.title: A Craftsman's Lacquer
sections.body: In Darnassus, armorer Mathiel studies methods pioneered by his colleague, the dwarf smith Furen Longbeard. Mathiel processes the shells into a fine lacquer for mail armor. Applied to the metal links, the coating strengthens them without burdening the wearer.

faq.answer: You can find them beneath wyvern nests across Highperch, a high mesa rising from the canyon floor in western Thousand Needles.

faq.q: What creature do these shells come from?
faq.answer: They are broken eggshells from the Highperch wyverns that roost atop the plateaus in Thousand Needles.

faq.q: Why does Mathiel want Sunscorched Shells?
faq.answer: Mathiel wants to test armorsmithing methods discovered by Furen Longbeard. He renders the hardened shells into a tough lacquer to reinforce mail links.

faq.q: Who is Furen Longbeard and how is he involved?
faq.answer: Furen Longbeard is an iron-working colleague of Mathiel, based in Stormwind's Dwarven District. His experiments with unusual reagents and hardening methods inspired Mathiel to try lacquer made from wyvern shells.

angles.text: As a warrior seeking mail protection, you can help Mathiel gather durable eggshells for reinforced armor.
As a blacksmith, you can see how skilled smiths use natural mineral coatings to make protective lacquer for linked armor.
